main_text.p: XXVI. Præceptores & patronos meos omnes, si modò quid iubere possum, saluere iubeo.

Ad[?] vero animo mentēq; comprehensa, quod attinet: laudaturus per literas artes, virtutes, magistratum, & id genus alia: argumenta ex causis, effectis, adiunctis, contrariis promet, & laude atque celebratione digna ea esse oftendet: quia honesta: quia utilia ac eiusmodi, ut care rei illis, aut nō omnino, aut ægrè admodū genus humanū posit: quia magna cum voluptate atque delectatione coniuncta: quia mediocri adhibito studio comparari queant: aut si difficilia, vel hoc maximè nomine & laudanda, & excolenda, quod, Græcorum habet proverbium, χαλεπὰ τὰ καλά[?], quæ pulchra & difficilia esse soleant.

Tractatio ita instituitur: ut Exordium scribendi occasiones atq; causas contineat: propositio ἐπίδειξιν[?] laudationem habeat: confirmatio eiusdē rationes & argumenta complectatur: conclusio breui præcipuorum repetitione, atq; [illegible, ~6 letters] adhortatione absoluatur. Nos exercitij gratia co-iugij in manus laudationem sumemus.

p.i: I. Audio ita studijs te incubere muneriq; impofito vacare, ut de contrahendo matrimonio curam atq; cogitationem nullam fuscipias: imò odio quoq; eos

page.notes: Uncertain readings: the sign after "Ad" at the start of the second paragraph; the Greek proverb after "habet proverbium" (read as χαλεπὰ τὰ καλά, unverified); the Greek word after "propositio" (read as ἐπίδειξιν, unverified); the word group after "atq;" in the conclusion sentence is illegible. Printed "imposito" appears as "impofito" and "suscipias" as "fuscipias"; kept as printed in the long-s form. Running head is LAVDATORIIS. printed with V for vowel u; normalised to LAUDATORIIS. The "m 3" at the foot is a gathering signature.
